statement: Is every connected bipartite graph in which all vertices of the same part have the same degree Sidorenko?

source.reference: Hatami (2010) proves that a weakly norming graph is biregular; the 2026 counterexample pins its types by colour refinement, which is stable from the first step on every biregular graph; K_{5,5} minus C_10, which Hatami (2010) and Conlon and Lee (2021) name as the smallest graph for which the conjecture is open, is 3-regular.

observation: On a biregular bipartite graph the first refinement step gives every vertex of a part the same neighbour-colour histogram, so the pinning lemma of the counterexample never applies, while biregularity is the necessary condition of the norming method. The class contains K_{5,5} minus C_10 and every odd twisted blow-up C_{2k+1}^bowtie, which this record identifies with the incidence graphs of the triangulated Mobius bands.
neighbours: Is every odd twisted blow-up $C_{2k+1}^{\bowtie}$ Sidorenko?
Is every connected edge-transitive bipartite graph Sidorenko?
Is every regular bipartite graph Sidorenko?
notes: The class contains the long-standing smallest open case, so a resolution would settle it.
